The `source` array points to a predictable GitHub release tarball using a version tag (v1.0.0), along with local files that will be included in the package build. While two of the sources have 'SKIP' checksums, this is not a concern for this phase, as the commands in question are intended to fetch and extract sources regardless of verification — the actual execution of extracted code is prevented by `--nobuild` and `--noprepare`. No network requests or file operations outside of expected source fetching occur during the sourcing of this PKGBUILD.
</details>

This supports reproducibility and reduces supply-chain risk. </details>

The systemd service and sysusers.d entries suggest the package sets up a dedicated user and system integration, which is normal for daemons. data.reasoning: The package is a standard AUR package with no malicious indicators. The PKGBUILD has no dangerous top-level code, the main source tarball is pinned with SHA256, local files (service, sysusers, conf) are standard systemd/config files with no executable content, and there are no .install hooks or suspicious network operations. The disagreement was caused solely by a model error in deepseek-v4-flash, not by substantive security concerns.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is artificial - caused by a tool/model error in deepseek-v4-flash where the LLM returned an empty response for mpxcast.sysusers, forcing an inconclusive verdict. The qwen model reviewed all 7 files successfully and found no issues. Both models agreed on the safety of all other files.
coverage_issues: deepseek-v4-flash failed to produce a verdict for mpxcast.sysusers due to LLMResponseError (empty response)
learnings: Model errors (empty responses, timeouts) should not force an inconclusive verdict when other models have successfully reviewed the same files - implement fallback logic or error recovery
When a single file causes inconclusive due to model error, the audit tool should retry that specific file or defer to other models' assessments
Distinguish between 'model failed to analyze' and 'file is suspicious' - these require different handling in verdict aggregation
